cue: How do you tell someone to stop forcing it and let it develop?

es.meaning: To let matters take their course instead of forcing them.
es.example: No la presiones con la respuesta; hay que dar tiempo al tiempo.
es.exampleTranslation: Don't push her for an answer — you have to let it take its course.

it.meaning: To let matters take their course instead of forcing them.
it.example: Non insistere per una risposta; bisogna dare tempo al tempo.
it.exampleTranslation: Don't push for an answer — you have to let it take its course.

bridge.note: Four words, four matches, no divergence at all in the infinitive. The trap appears only when Italian puts it in the imperative, which is how the phrase is most often heard: dai tempo al tempo. That dai is one of the busiest strings in Italian — the imperative of dare, the contraction of da + i, and the standalone interjection meaning come on — and a Spanish speaker meeting it inside a proverb has no way to know which one is being used.

interference.es_to_it: The imperative is dai, not 'da' — and it is not the preposition. Spanish's own imperative is da tiempo al tiempo, one letter short of the Italian, which makes the Italian look like a typo rather than a different word.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish has no equivalent of the dai ambiguity: its imperative is simply da. Watch the noun instead — Spanish tiempo covers both time and weather, exactly as Italian tempo does, so this pair is safe where the neighbouring vocabulary is not.
